Krichene and Rendle show that sampled ranking metrics can reverse model orderings relative to full-catalog metrics, even in expectation. Preserve the pinned HR@10 protocol: 200 users and 99 unique negatives per category, evaluation seed 42, equal category weighting. Improvements establish performance on this sampled benchmark; they do not establish better full-catalog top-10 retrieval, diversity, or satisfaction. Twenty simulator users provide qualitative diagnostics, not independent evidence of population-wide improvement. [Study](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)

For paired uncertainty, retain each model’s per-user hit indicator on identical candidates. Compute differences within users, then average within categories and across the four categories. Bootstrap paired users within each category, preserving category weights, to obtain an approximate 95% interval for the macro difference; report category differences and discordant hit counts too. One changed hit moves category HR by 0.5 percentage points and macro HR by 0.125 points. These intervals describe user-sampling uncertainty conditional on trained models and fixed candidates; they exclude training-seed variability, candidate-resampling variability, and selection bias. Dwork et al. explain why repeated adaptive validation undermines ordinary inferential guarantees. [Study](https://arxiv.org/abs/1506.02629)

Suggested prespecified schedule: baseline plus three single-factor SASRec ablations—dropout, weight decay, and training-negative sampling—with exact settings fixed beforehand. Keep preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, all categories, and the 200-epoch default; fix checkpoint evaluation times and selection rules. Allocate at most 9,000 GPU-seconds per configuration, including all category training, reserving 7,200 of 43,200 seconds for diagnostics/failures; shorten runs uniformly if necessary. Log every comparison, select by macro HR@10 with a predefined baseline-favoring tie rule, and avoid follow-up tuning. Fewer comparisons reduce overfitting but do not eliminate winner’s optimism.
